text:
incident-bot: Pager — Smart routing health probe oscillation detected for routing-policy. Affected targets: inference-proxy, model-variant-selection. Traffic is bouncing between us-east1 <-> us-west1 <-> eu-west1, causing increased 502s and retry storms across multiple customers. Paging oncall: @alice :pager:

alice: on it. grabbing logs and full routing map now.

fiona: I’m watching tracing — I can see continuous healthcheck flaps: us-east probes succeed, then fail, then us-west picks up and fails similarly, then eu flips. looks like probe sensitivity + transient infra restart on one host pool.

eric: Confirmed — there was a rolling kernel patch earlier in us-east that restarted a small subset of nodes ~3:07UTC, health checks drooped for ~20s windows. routing-policy has aggressive fallback (consecutive_failures=2, immediate cross-region fallback).

bob: That explains it. Routing policy is too chatty here. We should temporarily stop cross-region fallback to break the oscillation.

alice: Agreed. plan: 1) disable cross-region auto-fallback (set fallback_mode=regional-only) 2) bump consecutive_failures from 2 -> 5 3) pin model variant for affected customers to stable variant until probe stabilizes. Doing step 1 now (will run a controlled policy patch).

carla: Heads up — disabling fallback will keep traffic in region; if region saturates we'll need to enable burst capacity. monitoring dashboards up.

alice: running command:
```
# patch routing policy
curl -X PATCH https://control-plane.redwood.internal/api/v1/routing-policies/primary -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN' -d '{"fallback_mode":"regional-only"}'
```

alice: patched fallback_mode -> regional-only. forcing policy reload on proxies.

fiona: seeing policy refresh across proxies. health-check flaps still visible but retries no longer triggering cross-region swing. 502 rate dropping.

dave: CS: we have two customers reporting increased 5xx rates in EU (tickets #5912, #5915). I've messaged them that we're actively mitigating and will update in 15m.

eric: next change: bump consecutive failures and increase healthcheck-grace to 30s. applying now via infra playbook.
```
# playbook excerpt
kubectl -n infra patch configmap health-probe-config --patch '{"data":{"consecutive_failures":"5","grace_seconds":"30"}}'
```

eric: applied. pushing to proxies; should reduce noise from short restarts.

bob: pinning model variant for the two affected customers to `rwd-stable-3b` to avoid variant mismatch fallback.

bob: command:
```
POST /api/v1/customers/ACME/overrides
{ "pin_model":"rwd-stable-3b", "ttl_seconds":3600 }
```

bob: pinned for 1h.

fiona: Monitoring: 5xxs trending down to baseline over last 4 minutes. Latency stable. retry loops stopped.

alice: good. severity set to SEV2 while we watch. incident-bot, flag for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1830123456, severity SEV2. Postmortem required. Notifying oncall rotation and recording timeline.

carla: Note: we saw a small capacity pressure in us-east after disabling fallback, but autoscaler kicked in within 2min. no customer-visible dropped connections.

ops-bot: Automated note: deploy wave in us-east at 03:07UTC triggered 12 node restarts — linked runbook -> https://runbooks.redwood.internal/health-probe-oscillation

dave: CS update: both customers ack'd the update and will keep incidents open until the next update. good to mention we'll share root cause and mitigation timeline.

eric: rolling back the aggressive fallback change to permanent config will need a follow-up patch — we should tune default consecutive_failures to 4 and grace to 20s in the next config release.

bob: agreed. Also adding a safeguard: when fallback_mode changes, add a 60s cooldown to prevent immediate re-fallback toggles.

alice: handing off monitoring to bob for the night shift. I'll file the incident timeline and action items.

bob: taking over. I’ll keep an eye for 2 hours, then hand to next rotation. leaving an action item: ACTION: infra to add cooldown, ACTION: SRE to update runbook with the new thresholds, ACTION: ENG to review kernel patch process for noisy restarts.

fiona: can we also add a synthetic that simulates health-probe flaps to detect dangerous routing configs?

alice: good idea — add to postmortem.

incident-bot: Closure criteria met (retries stopped, 5xx down to baseline). Incident remains open for postmortem until next week.

bob: thanks team. I'll post a short incident summary in #incidents-summary and ping stakeholders.

alice: TL;DR — root cause: rolling infra restart in us-east caused short transient failures; routing-policy was configured to failover too aggressively causing oscillation; mitigation: temporarily disabled cross-region fallback, increased probe thresholds, pinned variants, autoscaler absorbed load. Postmortem to cover permanent config changes and safeguards.

dave: noted. I'll coordinate customer post-incident emails tomorrow morning.

fiona: monitoring looks quiet. setting alert to notify if 502 rate > 2x baseline in any region for 5m.

bob: handoff complete. ping me if anything spikes.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation. Postmortem task created: TASK-3921.
